items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: And he did it with Jon Kellso too, the young trumpet player in New York. Kellso had a similar dream.

ctx.x: Kind of funny, like hearing him play in these dreams. And he talked to me. Oh it was really weird. And he did it with Jon Kellso too, the young trumpet player in New York. Kellso had a similar dream. Like it makes me cry to think about it. He said he was sitting on a park bench and he saw Louis sitting on this other park bench, and then Louis got up in this dream and walked over the just sat down by him and took his hand and just kind of patted his hand. Like, you know, don’t worry about a thing, everything’s…

That’s got to be like the best dream you could have I think. When I was a little kid, it was about 1963 or something like that, Louis Armstrong came to New Orleans. And this big brass band like George Lewis and Punch Miller and my dad and everybody went out there to meet Louis. And my dad told my brother and I said, “look, get some clothes on, I’m going to take you someplace” you know and we were wondering where we were going. He said, “I’m going to take you see Louis Armstrong.” I really didn’t think I would see…
